title: Dedicated capacity weekly sync - prep notes (1:1 + forecast)
content:
Purpose: prep for weekly dedicated-capacity sync + 1:1 with Priya. Capture current pool forecasts, ask for commit changes, follow-ups on autoscaling tests and priority routings.

Meeting goals:
- Align on Q2 committed reservations vs current utilization and forecast for Q3 ramp.
- Confirm autoscaling policy changes we want to pilot (burst headroom, cold-start limits).
- Decide on immediate action items: reservations to purchase/convert, canary for new eviction policy.

Quick status (as of 2026-03-02):
- Pools:
  - pool-a-prod (A100s, nvlink): reserved 48 units (monthly commit). Current avg util last 7d: 64% tokens/sec (target 60-70%). Peak 85% during batch jobs on Tue morning.
  - pool-b-batch (A10s): reserved 16, currently underutilized ~28% (spikes for nightly retrievers).
  - pool-c-temp (T4/spot-like): 24 ephemeral, used for dev and internal evals; eviction rate ~6% last 30d.
- Cost: committed discounts covering ~70% of A100 hours; overspend occurs when burst uses on-demand A100s (~$Xk last month).
- Incidents: one latency spike (2026-02-25) due to autoscale hang when scaling >8 instances simultaneously; SRE ticket INF-789 open, root cause likely race in scaler state machine.

Forecast notes (Q2 -> mid Q3):
- Product signals: 2 enterprise trials expect to go GA in May (combined expected sustained +200 A100-hours/day).
- Expected baseline growth: ~10% month-over-month across hosted->dedicated migrations.
- Conservative reserve ask for next commit window: +12 A100 (convert from ephemeral pool-c) to bring pool-a to 60 reserved. Rationale: keep steady-state util in 60-70% band while reducing on-demand spend.

Autoscaling proposals to discuss:
1) Increase max burst for pool-a from +20% to +30% for 90s window to reduce tail latency on short spikes (tradeoff: more on-demand spend).
2) Introduce queue-depth-aware scaling: prefer gradual scale up for >100 concurrent requests rather than instant spin-up to N nodes. Helps avoid scaler race.
3) Canary policy: enable new eviction/backfill logic on pool-c for 7 days, route 10% of internal eval traffic through canary.

Questions for Priya (1:1):
- Can we push the conversion of 12 A100s from ephemeral to reserved in the March commit? What approvals are needed (finance/contract)?
- Prioritization: if we cannot reserve, prioritize which workloads we shift off A100 during peak window? (options: nightly retrievers, large-batch evals, internal dev runs).
- Timeline for INF-789 fix and deployment: do we have an ETA for the scaler state machine patch? Any risk for next week's planned load test?

Action items (pre-meeting / to bring up):
- [Samir] Prepare cost delta spreadsheet for +12 A100 reservation vs current on-demand spend (due 2026-03-03). Link in ticket.
- [Liam] Run autoscaling stress test (scale from 0 -> 32 nodes) in staging, capture logs, and verify scaler fix branch. Share results by 2026-03-04.
- [Priya] Check with finance on ability to convert ephemeral to reserved mid-cycle; confirm steps and lead time.
- [SRE] Keep INF-789 owner assigned and PR ready for canary deployment; prioritize review.

Notes / talking points (short):
- Emphasize predictability for enterprise customers: reserved capacity request is primarily about SLA and tail latency guarantees.
- Show cost tradeoffs: slightly higher reservation = lower on-demand tail spend + simpler routing.
- Mention rollout plan: reserve first, then change routing policies to reduce autoscale pressure for 2 weeks, monitor cost and latency.

Follow-ups (post-meeting expected):
- Finalize commit change and send PO to procurement (if approved).
- Schedule 10% canary for new eviction logic and monitor eviction metrics (eviction-rate, failed-inference, cold-start-latency).
- Update Runbook section: "reserved vs burst policy" with new thresholds and contacts.

Misc / notes to self:
- Bring up GitHub PR #214 (runtime scaler patch) during sync, ask for review from SRE and infra.
- Prep a 1-slide cost vs latency chart showing current month + projected with +12 A100s.
- Slack threads to reference: #dedicated-capacity (link pinned) and #sre-incidents.

End of prep. Will iterate after 1:1.
